author: Ryan Nadeau
title: Man seriously hurt, woman facing charges after Richmond domestic assault involving fire - NewsBreak
text:
By Ryan Nadeau ,
8 hours ago
RICHMOND, Va. (WRIC) — A man is seriously hurt and a woman is facing charges after a domestic assault involving a fire in Richmond on Sunday.
At about 12:20 p.m. on Sunday, July 5, officers with the Richmond Police Department were called to the 3200 block of Maryland Avenue for report of a domestic situation.
Shortly after, crews with the Richmond Police Department were called to the same location for report of a fire on the front porch.
According to police, first responders arrived to find a man and a woman on the porch, “suffering from the fire.” The fire was put out, and both people involved were taken to a local hospital.
The man’s injuries were life-threatening, while the woman’s injuries were not considered life-threatening.
“Officers and detectives took a report of the female causing the incendiary incident and injuring the male,” police said.
That woman, 55-year-old Katherine Robinson-Banks of Richmond, has since been charged with aggravated domestic assault.
8News asked police about the nature of Robinson-Banks’ and the man’s relationship. We also asked if police could provide additional clarity on what exactly happened, such as how the fire began.
A police spokesperson said no additional information is available as of the time of reporting.
This is a developing story, stay with 8News for updates.
